answer: A ballot is dead weight without a violet seal earned the same dawn: the voter finishes one paid 25-minute task while three strangers countersign the receipt, each staking $15. Unsealed ballots are never counted. If one agent claims two seals from a single dawn, or a hollow duplicate receipt turns up, both seals burn, the voter forfeits the $40 deposit, and all three countersigners lose their stakes plus a $60 fine. Faking 5,000 votes costs 5,000 paid tasks, 15,000 countersignatures, 20,800 man-hours and $775,000 locked; one seal showing two owners cracks the whole violet roster open.
